name: Chandrasekhara Venkata Raman (C.V. Raman)
summary: Indian physicist renowned for the discovery of the Raman effect and contributions to light scattering and acoustics.

name: Parvathi Ammal
summary: Mother of C. V. Raman.

name: R. Chandrasekhara Iyer
summary: Father of C. V. Raman, a school teacher and lecturer in mathematics and physics.

name: Lokasundari Ammal
summary: Wife of C. V. Raman.

name: K. S. Krishnan
summary: Physicist and collaborator of C. V. Raman on the discovery of Raman scattering.

name: Nagendra Nath
summary: Student and collaborator of C. V. Raman on acousto-optics.

name: G. N. Ramachandran
summary: Student of C. V. Raman who reported on optical fluctuation and speckles.

name: S. Pancharatnam
summary: Physicist mentored by C. V. Raman, known for work on optical phase.

name: Max Born
summary: Physicist who had a technical disagreement with Raman on crystal lattice dynamics.

name: Arthur Compton
summary: Physicist whose X-ray scattering observations motivated Raman's work on light scattering.

name: Mandelstam
summary: Physicist who made contemporary contributions to inelastic scattering of light in solids.

name: Presidency College
summary: College in Madras where Raman completed his undergraduate and master's degrees.

name: Indian Financial Service
summary: Government service where Raman worked as Assistant Accountant General before becoming a professor.

aliases: Indian Association of Cultivation of Science
name: Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science
summary: Research institution in Calcutta where Raman performed independent research while employed in financial service.

name: Calcutta University
summary: University where Raman became a professor in 1917.

name: Indian Institute of Science
summary: Institute in Bangalore where Raman served as Director and later Professor.

name: Raman Research Institute
summary: Institute in Bangalore founded and directed by Raman from 1948 until his death.

name: Thiruvanaikkaval
summary: Town in Tamil Nadu, India, where C. V. Raman was born.

name: Tamil Nadu
summary: Southern state of India where Thiruvanaikkaval is located.

name: Madras
summary: City in India where Raman studied and began his career.

name: Calcutta
summary: City in eastern India where Raman worked for many years.

name: Bangalore
summary: City in India where Raman worked at IISc and RRI, and where he died.

name: Europe
summary: Continent Raman visited in 1921, inspiring his work on light scattering.

name: Mediterranean Sea
summary: Sea whose blue color inspired Raman's research on light scattering.

name: Raman Effect
summary: Phenomenon of inelastic scattering of light discovered by C. V. Raman.

name: Nobel Prize in Physics
summary: Prestigious award won by C. V. Raman in 1930.

name: The Physiology of Vision
summary: Monograph by C. V. Raman on the optics of human vision.
